done.what: Materials keep who changed them last. FIRST THING: `studio_materials.updated_by` in lib/db/schema.ts plus the additive migration drizzle/0056_materials_updated_by.sql (`ALTER TABLE studio_materials ADD updated_by text`, made with drizzle-kit generate, nothing else in it). updateStudioMaterial and renameStudioMaterial now stamp it through actingMember(). A rename to the same name is no change and returns early, so it doesn't stamp. A restore keeps both updated_at and updated_by (F125). A new material or a duplicate has none, so the card names whoever added it. MaterialRow carries `editedBy: string | null`, the member's name. Repair check added: 'studio material last changed by someone not on the team (wave E, E5)'.

FIRST THING: `export async function countLiveRenderLinks(leadId: string | readonly string[]): Promise<number>` in lib/visualizer/queries.ts (server-only). It counts the lead's client render links a client can open today: not stopped, not expired, the design not in the trash, something still on the link, the lead still with the studio. It goes through readShareLink, so it answers exactly as the /renders page would. Each link counts once, and an array works for a bulk delete. Checked: Kevin Ng = 1; [kevin, kevin, 'nope'] = 1; [] = 0; lead deleted = 0; lead restored = 1; link stopped = 0. The dialog line itself is the leads package's (see crossFileRequests).

The client link names members in full. `senderFirst` (data.sender.split(' ')[0]) is replaced by the whole stored name (`data.sender.trim() || studio name`) everywhere on the page: the how-to line, the 'n designs … shared earlier' note, the favourite, note and pin snackbars, the pin draft's hint, the refusal snackbars ('ask Hui Min for an updated one'), the call-back ask line and its done card ('Hui Min will call you back'). RenderLinkClosed now reads 'Please ask Hui Min at Demo Studio Pte Ltd for an updated link.' closedLinkError / closedLinkMessage and shareMeta already used the full name.

The client's renders page no longer uses the app rail's 84 px snackbar offset. app/renders/layout.tsx wraps the SnackbarProvider in `.snackFrame` (display: contents; `--rail-w: calc(max(0px, (100% - 928px) / 2) - 8px)`). The house host's `left: calc(var(--rail-w) + 32px)` then lands on the column's content edge, where the cards start. The 100% resolves in the fixed host's own `left`, so it is the window without its scrollbar. At ≤767 the house's 16 px gutters still apply. Measured on a static replica with Playwright: card and snackbar both start at 280 (1440), 200 (1280), 72.5 (1025), 24 (900 and 768), with no sideways scroll.

The client page says 'Click' to a mouse and 'Tap' to a finger, using the editor's check (useMediaQuery('(hover: none)')). This covers the intro line ('Click I like this one on your favourite…') and the pin hint ('Click the picture where you’d like a change'). The server snapshot renders 'Click' and a touch device switches after hydration, as in the editor.
/sign/[id]/quote for a contract that is gone or was never made now returns the house notice <LinkGone studio brand> (fetchBrand), as /sign/[id] does, instead of Next's bare 404.

Server half of E12: Rename and Change photo follow the Delete-room rule (the room's maker, the design's maker, an Owner or an Admin). renameRoom, setRoomPhoto and undoRoomPhoto refuse with the rule before doing anything. The rule now names all three actions, so the menu can say it once: ROOM_RULE = 'Only whoever made it or its design, an Owner or an Admin can rename this room, change its photo or delete it'. roomChangeBlock is exported as an alias of roomDeleteBlock. EditorRoom carries `mayChange: string | null`, the same value as mayDelete. Checked as Sarah (Designer): rename Dane's room, rename Michelle's room, set photo and undo photo each come back with the rule. As Michelle, renaming her own room works.

(a) The AI Visualizer folder rule names its maker: new ownFolderRule(maker) = 'Only Dane, an Owner or an Admin can rename, move or delete this folder'. folderChangeBlockFor takes an optional 4th `maker` argument, and fetchVisualizerHome passes the folder maker's name. OWN_FOLDER_RULE is kept as the nameless fallback. (b) A lead's design never offers Move or Rename, so its rule says only Delete: designRule(maker, fixed) / designChangeBlock(v, createdBy, maker, fixed). The gallery card, the editor's design.mayChange and deleteDesigns' refusal all pass kind === 'lead', giving 'Only Dane, an Owner or an Admin can delete this'. A personal design keeps 'can move, rename or delete this'. Checked as Sarah in fetchVisualizerHome and deleteDesigns.

Server half for a deleted lead's design. VisualizerEditorData carries `leadDeleted` at the top level and in `design.leadDeleted`: true when the lead is in the leads' trash or its row is gone. `lead` still carries the name for the top bar. saveVersionToFiles, addVersionToQuote and createShareLink refuse with the new policy words `leadDeletedNote(name)` = 'Kevin Ng was deleted — restore the lead to share, file or quote from this design.'. `LEAD_DELETED_ROW` = 'Its lead was deleted' is exported for the editor's greyed rows. Checked: editor leadDeleted true (leadClosed true too), and all three actions refuse with the note.

A render filed in Files › Renders gets a free name when its name is taken: 'Render - Kitchen - V1 (2).jpg' (new pure freeFileName(name, taken) in lib/visualizer/outputs.ts, case-insensitive against the folder's live files). This applies to Save to Files and to the filing that Share with client does. The legacy match by name is untouched, so a render already filed is still found as before ('again' → existed: true, same file). Downloads keep the plain name. Checked with a same-named foreign file in Kevin's Renders.

Material usage is split into two counts on MaterialRow. `renderedIn` = designs where a version was made with the material, so their renders keep it. `waitingIn` = designs where it is only picked and waiting for Generate, with no render of it in that design. `usedIn` = renderedIn + waitingIn, the same total as before. Checked: a pick of Sage Whisper in the bedroom's picks, never generated, gives usedIn 1 · renderedIn 0 · waitingIn 1. The wording belongs to the gallery package.

Server/shared half: plainFinishName names a reference colour among the surface's own kind of finish. The kind comes through the surface group, as the Surfaces list and the version lines group it (groupMaterialCategories(surfaceGroupFor(label))), then the label's own words (resolveSurfaceCategories), then Paints. Wallpapers never name a flat colour. A painted surface (walls, ceiling, trim) stays with the paints. A hard surface looks on through its other kinds before giving up: worktops → Countertops then Stone, splashbacks → Tiles, Glass, Stone, floors → Flooring, Tiles, Stone. 'Quartz Island Waterfall End' was 'close to Linen' (a paint) and now names a quartz or stone. Checked with a tsx table over six colours and the kitchen's labels, e.g. #E8E6E2 gives worktops and island → Quartz Calacatta, backsplash → Hexagon Marble, walls and ceiling → Off-White Matte, floor → Marble White Polished. Moodboard grouping by the resolved name is the canvas package's (crossFileRequest).

Part (b), server and shared half: new noQuoteReason(v, lines) in lib/visualizer/outputs.ts. A whole-room look (restyle, or a version wearing a style) reads 'A whole-room look has no finishes to quote — pick finishes on the Original'. Anything else reads 'This version has no finishes to quote — pick finishes, then Generate'. addVersionToQuote refuses with it (plus a full stop) instead of '…to quote yet.' Checked on the Kitchen's Scandinavian V1. Part (a), the note caveat, is the engine package's; the menu row is the editor package's.

db:repair no longer fails its own checks after the studio deletes demo records. 'AI Visualizer demo design missing' now looks for any design of Kevin Ng's, including one in the trash. A design deleted for good is written again by R61's fixed ids, so only 'no design at all' counts as missing. 'demo folder with nothing filed in it' now counts entries in the trash as filed, in every library, because they keep their folder and a Restore puts them back. Reproduced on a private copy (Showroom concept, Kevin's design and Walnut vinyl moved to the trash): FAIL ×2 before, 'all checks pass' after. On a fresh baseline copy the repair passes and a second run is byte-identical (sqlite .dump md5 equal).

Parity map 17 already says (line 18, 'The studio's picture routes need a signed-in session … a request with no session must get a 401'), but without the word 'authenticated' the verifier's grep for 'authenticat' missed it. Both picture routes now also carry a PRODUCTION comment ('needs an authenticated session — no session, a 401 before these checks run'), so a grep in the code finds it too. No behaviour change.

notDone.why: E9 decides it: Download stays one JPEG per version. PNG, full resolution, Download all as a zip and a brand-kit mark remain proposals for the owner.

Not fixed: if the studio deletes one of R59's seeded templates for good, or moves every seeded entry out of a demo folder, the REG-664 check can still flag that folder. R61's own folders don't have this problem, because R61 re-seeds by fixed ids. The case reported (soft delete) is fixed.

Only waitingIn > 0 → 'Picked in {waitingIn} design(s), not rendered yet — the pick comes back if you restore it.'. Both → the two sentences one after the other. usedIn is still the total.
